responsibility: Sequence acquisition -> enrichment -> analysis for one run. Create the run row, run the parameter-consistency preflight, maintain per-stage status in run_stages, emit run_events progress records, service cooperative cancellation, translate every exception into a terminal run status, and keep all of that off the Streamlit script thread.
design_notes: This module is the only place that knows the pipeline order. The three stage modules do not import each other and do not import this module (ADR-009).

Resume is stage-granular and happens in place on the same run_id, backed by the run_stages table (ADR-014). A new run_id would re-fetch the entire SteamSpy catalog, because the raw payload cache is keyed by run_id and there is no cross-run reuse path in v1.
Cancellation is cooperative and checked at a fixed, enumerated set of points, never by killing a thread (ADR-015).
The run status vocabulary is not extended. Partial completion is expressed by run_stages plus reporting.is_partial (ADR-016).
No sqlite3.Connection ever crosses a thread boundary. The async entry points take a Path (ADR-017).
Every numeric constant reaching a stage comes from config; this module passes parameter objects through and never defaults them.

public_interface.name: PipelineStage
public_interface.description: Declaration order is execution order, so list(PipelineStage) is the pipeline. Values are byte-identical to the run_events.stage and run_stages.stage strings and to the stage names in the run_stages CHECK constraint.

public_interface.name: RUN_LEVEL_STAGE
public_interface.description: The run_events.stage value used for run-level records (preflight, run started, run finished, cancellation requested). Deliberately not a PipelineStage member because it is not executable and must never appear in run_stages.

public_interface.name: PipelineConfig
public_interface.description: Only what varies per run and is not a formulation parameter. Everything in FORMULATION.md reaches the pipeline through config/parameters.toml and is not settable here or from the UI. start_stage drives both resume and a deliberate stage re-run after a parameter change. max_catalog_pages is the smoke-test limiter already present in acquisition.fetch_steamspy_catalog. request_budget_override supersedes AcquisitionConfig.request_budget when set and is None otherwise. notes is free user text persisted to the existing runs.notes column. Serialized into runs.config_json via to_dict/from_dict.

public_interface.name: run_pipeline
public_interface.signature: def run_pipeline(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, config: PipelineConfig, *, settings: Settings | None = None, cancel_token: threading.Event | None = None) -> PipelineResult
public_interface.description: Synchronous execution on the caller's thread using the caller's connection, which the caller owns and closes. Loads settings and parameters, runs the ADR-013 preflight, then executes each stage from config.start_stage to the end of the enum. Records terminal status for both the stage and the run, then re-raises, so tests and any future CLI caller observe the original exception. This is the function the worker thread calls.

public_interface.name: start_pipeline_async
public_interface.signature: def start_pipeline_async(db_path: Path, config: PipelineConfig, *, settings: Settings | None = None) -> str
public_interface.description: Creates the run row on the calling thread through a short-lived connection, registers a cancellation token, starts a non-daemon worker thread, and returns run_id immediately so the UI can begin polling. Never accepts and never returns a sqlite3.Connection. The worker opens its own connection as its first statement and closes it in a finally. The worker catches every exception rather than re-raising, because an exception escaping a thread target is invisible.

public_interface.name: resume_run
public_interface.signature: def resume_run(db_path: Path, run_id: str, *, settings: Settings | None = None) -> str
public_interface.description: Resumes an existing run in place. Reads run_stages, finds the first stage in pipeline order whose status is not 'succeeded', rebuilds PipelineConfig from runs.config_json with start_stage set to that stage, then starts a worker exactly as start_pipeline_async does. Returns the same run_id: no new run row, no new run_id, and parent_run_id is untouched. Raises PipelineError if the run is unknown, is already running, or has all three stages succeeded.

public_interface.name: cancel_run
public_interface.description: Sets the in-process cancellation event for run_id and appends a RUN_LEVEL_STAGE event recording the request. Returns False as an idempotent no-op when no live worker is registered for that run_id. Does not block waiting for the worker to stop and does not itself change runs.status; the worker writes the 'cancelled' status when it unwinds.

public_interface.name: is_running
public_interface.description: True when a live worker thread is registered for run_id in this process.

public_interface.name: active_run_ids
public_interface.description: Run ids with a live worker. Used by the UI to decide whether to offer Cancel or Resume, and by reconcile_orphaned_runs.

public_interface.name: reconcile_orphaned_runs
public_interface.description: Called once at UI startup. Any run whose runs.status is 'pending' or 'running' but which has no live worker in this process is marked failed with error_message 'process terminated before completion', and any of its run_stages rows left at 'running' are marked failed likewise. Returns the reconciled run ids. This is what makes a run killed by a process restart resumable rather than permanently stuck.

public_interface.name: make_event_sink
public_interface.signature: def make_event_sink(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, *, cancel_token: threading.Event | None = None) -> EventSink
public_interface.description: Builds the concrete storage.EventSink the stage entry points receive. Wraps storage.append_run_event, adds throttling so a per-app loop cannot write one row per request, and is the single place that decides event granularity.

public_interface.name: PipelineError
public_interface.description: Base for this module. Raised for invalid resume requests and other orchestration-level misuse.

public_interface.name: PipelineCancelled
public_interface.description: Subclass of PipelineError. Raised at a cancellation check-point. Carries the stage it was raised in.

public_interface.name: PreflightError
public_interface.description: Subclass of PipelineError. Raised when the ADR-013 parameters.toml / FORMULATION.md consistency check fails, or when config.load_parameters raises ParameterError. Raised after the run row exists so the failure is visible in the run list, but before any stage begins.

per_stage_sequence: call the stage entry point with the shared EventSink and cancel token
let the stage commit its own data writes
append a stage-complete run_event, last of all
preflight: storage.create_run (run row exists before anything can fail, so every failure is visible in the run list)
parameters.toml / FORMULATION.md consistency check (ADR-013) - runs on resume too, so a resume cannot silently continue against a hand-edited parameter file
storage.initialize_schema / migrate to the current version

stage_entry_points.acquisition: acquisition.run_acquisition(conn, run_id, acquisition_config, settings, on_event=sink) -> AcquisitionReport
stage_entry_points.enrichment: enrichment.run_enrichment(conn, run_id, enrichment_params, parameters_version=..., on_event=sink) -> EnrichmentReport
stage_entry_points.analysis: analysis.run_analysis(conn, run_id, analysis_params, parameters_version=..., on_event=sink) -> AnalysisReport

cancellation.mechanism: A module-level registry _CANCEL_REGISTRY: dict[str, threading.Event] guarded by a threading.Lock, populated by start_pipeline_async / resume_run and removed in the worker's finally. In-memory is sufficient because ADR-002 and ADR-006 put the UI and the pipeline in one process; if the process dies the run dies with it and reconcile_orphaned_runs cleans up.
checkpoints: CP1 - run_pipeline, immediately before each stage begins, after the previous stage's run_stages row is committed
CP2 - acquisition SteamSpy bulk loop, after each page's payloads are persisted and committed, before the next RateLimiter.acquire()
CP3 - acquisition appdetails loop, after each batch of appids is persisted and committed, before the next batch's first RateLimiter.acquire()
CP4 - acquisition review-summary loop, identical placement to CP3

CP5 - inside RateLimiter.acquire(), whose wait is implemented as cancel_token.wait(remaining_interval); if it wakes because of cancellation it raises PipelineCancelled before consuming a token and before any socket is opened
CP6 - enrichment, between processed chunks of the feature frame
CP7 - analysis, between named sub-steps: simplicity filter, cluster_tags, compute_demand, compute_competition_density, compute_tag_trends, build_opportunity_matrix
safety_rules: Cancellation is never checked between RateLimiter.acquire() returning and the request being issued; a consumed token is always spent on a real request
An in-flight HTTP request is never aborted. The response body is always read to completion so the pooled connection is returned to the session clean
The only interruptible wait is CP5, and it raises before the request is issued, so no partially-sent request can exist
Every check-point sits after a committed unit of work, so cancellation never discards data that the UI has already been told about
cancellation.latency_bound: Worst-case time from cancel_run to the worker unwinding is one in-flight HTTP request timeout plus one batch persist. Both are bounded by Settings.http_timeout_seconds and the batch size, so the UI can state a bound rather than an indefinite wait.
cancellation.unwind: PipelineCancelled propagates to run_pipeline, whose finally writes finish_run_stage(stage, 'cancelled') and update_run_status(run_id, 'cancelled'). Committed partial data is kept, never rolled back, and the run remains resumable.

terminal_status_mapping.note: status is written, then the BaseException is re-raised so the interpreter still exits

terminal_status_mapping.exception: PreflightError (wraps ParameterError or a parameter-consistency mismatch)
terminal_status_mapping.error_message: the validation message naming the offending key

terminal_status_mapping.note: if the status write itself is the failing path, log to stderr and give up rather than looping

status_rules: error_message format is fixed: '{stage}: {ExceptionType}: {message}', truncated to a sane length. The full traceback is appended as a separate run_event at level 'error' rather than being squeezed into the column.
A run reaches 'succeeded' only when all three run_stages rows have status 'succeeded'.

No new runs.status value is introduced for partial success. Degraded-but-complete outcomes stay 'succeeded' and are surfaced numerically; incomplete outcomes are 'failed' or 'cancelled' and are surfaced through reporting.is_partial (ADR-016).
Per-app fetch failures inside a successful acquisition do not fail the run; they are reported through AcquisitionReport.detail_failed and reporting.FunnelSummary.
Exception: candidate_count > 0 while detail_fetched == 0 is a total acquisition failure, not an empty result. acquisition raises AcquisitionError and the run is 'failed'.
candidate_count == 0 after the coarse filter is a legitimate 'succeeded' run with empty downstream results and a warning event.

rules: A sqlite3.Connection never crosses a thread boundary. start_pipeline_async and resume_run take a Path and never accept or return a connection.
start_pipeline_async opens a short-lived connection on the calling thread to create the run row, commits, closes it, and only then starts the worker.
The worker thread's target opens its own connection with storage.connect() as its very first statement and closes it in a finally, around the run_pipeline call.
Worker threads are non-daemon so interpreter shutdown waits for a clean unwind and a terminal status write.
run_pipeline itself is connection-agnostic and thread-agnostic: it uses whatever connection it is handed, which is what makes the whole pipeline testable synchronously with no threads at all.
read_consistency: WAL gives the polling reader a snapshot of the last commit and stops readers and the writer from blocking each other, but it is necessary rather than sufficient.
Reader side: connections are autocommit and short-lived, one per Streamlit rerun. A long-lived open read transaction would pin a stale snapshot and polling would never advance.

Writer side: the data of a unit of work is committed before the run_events row or run_stages / runs status that announces it. Without this ordering, WAL would faithfully deliver a 'stage complete' event whose data is not yet committed, which is the actual torn-read hazard here.
Consequence the UI can rely on: any stage reported as 'succeeded' has all of its data already visible to a new reader.

invariants: The run row exists before any code that can fail runs, so no failure is invisible in the run list
Every stage transition is recorded in run_stages; a stage never runs without begin_run_stage first
finish_run_stage and update_run_status are the last writes of their unit of work, never the first
Cancellation is only ever observed at one of the seven enumerated check-points
A cancelled or failed run is left resumable: no committed data is rolled back on the way out
resume_run never creates a new run_id and never writes parent_run_id
This module contains no data transformation, no SQL and no HTTP call
The parameter-consistency preflight runs on every execution path, including resume
edge_cases: resume_run on a run with all three stages succeeded -> PipelineError; the user wants a new run, which is a different action
resume_run on a run already registered as running -> PipelineError, no second worker is started
resume_run on a run whose stages are all absent (created but never started) -> resumes from acquisition, which is the normal path after a crash during preflight

resume_run after parameters.toml changed since the original run -> preflight passes only if parameters.toml still matches FORMULATION.md; the resumed stages are stamped with the current parameters_version, so a resumed run can carry two parameters_version values across its derived rows. This is recorded as a warning event rather than blocked
cancel_run for an unknown or already-finished run -> returns False, no exception, no status change
cancel_run called twice -> second call is a no-op, the Event is already set
cancel_run arriving between two stages -> caught at CP1, the next stage never begins
cancel_run arriving during the preflight -> checked once after the preflight; the run ends 'cancelled' with no stage rows
Process killed mid-run -> runs.status stays 'running' until reconcile_orphaned_runs marks it failed at next startup, after which it is resumable
Two workers for the same run_id -> impossible by construction; registration into _CANCEL_REGISTRY is the mutual-exclusion point and happens under the lock before the thread starts

start_stage set to ANALYSIS on a run with no enriched rows -> the analysis stage handles an empty input per its own spec and succeeds with empty results plus a warning; orchestration does not pre-validate stage inputs
The stage entry point returns normally but wrote nothing (empty candidate set) -> 'succeeded', not 'failed'
storage.finish_run_stage raising while unwinding another exception -> the original exception is preserved and the storage failure is logged, never swallowing the root cause

unit: list(PipelineStage) is exactly the execution order and every value matches the run_stages CHECK constraint literals
PipelineConfig round-trips through to_dict / from_dict and through runs.config_json
run_pipeline with start_stage=ENRICHMENT never calls acquisition (stage entry points injected as stubs)
run_pipeline writes begin_run_stage before the stage call and finish_run_stage after it, in that order, asserted on a recording connection wrapper
the write-ordering rule holds: for each stage, the data write commit precedes the finish_run_stage commit which precedes the stage-complete event
each exception type in terminal_status_mapping produces exactly the specified runs.status and run_stages.status, driven by a parametrised stub stage that raises it
an unexpected Exception yields status 'failed' and the full traceback appears as an error-level run_event, not in runs.error_message
KeyboardInterrupt sets status 'cancelled' and is re-raised
a run reaches 'succeeded' only when all three stages succeeded; a stubbed two-of-three success yields 'failed'
PreflightError leaves the run row present, status 'failed', and no run_stages rows
cancellation at CP1 stops the pipeline before the next stage's begin_run_stage
a stub stage that polls the token at CP6/CP7 unwinds with status 'cancelled' and its committed rows survive
cancel_run returns False for an unknown run_id and True for a registered one, and is idempotent

RateLimiter CP5 behaviour: with a pre-set cancel token, acquire() raises PipelineCancelled without consuming a token and without issuing a request (asserted against a recording HTTP stub that must see zero calls)
resume_run picks the first non-succeeded stage for every combination of the three stage statuses (table-driven)
resume_run raises PipelineError for all-succeeded, unknown and already-running runs
resume_run returns the same run_id and creates no second run row
reconcile_orphaned_runs marks an orphaned 'running' run failed and leaves a genuinely live run untouched
start_pipeline_async never receives or returns a connection; passing one is a type error caught by the signature and asserted by a unit test on the worker's own connection identity
integration: a full three-stage run against stubbed HTTP and a temp database produces the expected run_stages rows, event sequence and terminal status
a run failed in enrichment, then resumed, completes without any further HTTP call being made (asserted on a recording HTTP stub that must see zero requests during the resume)
a run cancelled mid-acquisition and then resumed fetches only the appids that were still missing
testing.policy: No test may start a real network call, and no test may sleep on wall-clock time; the rate limiter's clock and wait are injected.

non_goals: No scheduler, no cron, no automatic re-crawl (ADR-006). trigger_type stays 'manual'
No cross-run incremental fetch; parent_run_id remains reserved and unused (ADR-014)
No within-stage checkpointing finer than 'appids already persisted for this run'
No parallel stages and no more than one live worker per run_id
No multi-process execution; the cancellation registry is in-process by design
No Streamlit import; the module must be runnable and testable headless
No business logic, no SQL, no HTTP
open_questions: Event throttling granularity in make_event_sink: one event per N apps or one per T seconds. Affects run_events table growth on a multi-thousand-app run
Whether a resumed run that spans two parameters_version values should be flagged in the UI more loudly than a warning event
